pairs.subject: delivery-guarantees
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/events.rs:197 An empty SSE replay ring is reported as a successful empty catch-up, so a client that reconnects after a restart with Last-Event-ID is not told the gap is gone and then drops every new event because sequence ids start again at 1.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:2511 Outcome updates match only the delivery id. A sender whose pending row was reclaimed can overwrite the reaper, and the claim UPDATE records no holder id.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:867 The handler effect is an HTTP POST outside the SQLite delivery row, so consume and effect cannot be one commit.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:2914 Aged dead rows are deleted with no non-delivery ledger write. The operator surface has replay and no discard or bulk verb.
crates/server/src/events.rs:196 The module promises reset when a gap has left the ring, but an empty ring after restart is treated as no loss. Webhook sends do keep a stable delivery id.
crates/server/src/events.rs:197 Empty means caught up. A stale Last-Event-ID then stays above every post-restart sequence id, so those events are never offered.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:471 A deliberate skip is a debug string. Governance audit rows cover executed actions, not this class of skip.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:808 Each delivery is its own row. A dead row is left out of the due scan; there is no keyed stream whose head wedges successors.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:2653 Manual replay increments the persisted counter instead of starting a new campaign, so an exhausted row that fails once is dead again. The drain ladder itself does move to status dead.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:2696 Pending rows older than the cutoff are returned to failed with a recorded reason. The next drain claim bumps retry_count, so a crash loop still reaches dead.

pairs.registryProposal: atomic-claiming requires a holder id and a conditional completion write, while stuck-reaping allows an age threshold when the claim has only a timestamp. A one-process delivery row that stores updated_at and reaps at a written multiple of worst-case send time cannot satisfy both texts; state which obligation is waived for a single process.
